lem-contrastive-hinge-and-logistic-loss-:
## Statement

Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm and $\log_2 u:=\ln(u)/\ln(2)$ for $u>0$. Define the one-negative hinge and logistic losses by $\ell_{\rm h}(t):=(1+t)_+$ and $\ell_{\rm log}(t):=\log_2(1+e^t)$ for $t\in\mathbb R$, where $r_+:=\max\{r,0\}$. Put $L_0:=1+1/\ln(2)$. Each loss is convex, nondecreasing, $L_0$-Lipschitz, and has value $1$ at $0$. For $R>0$ and either loss $\ell$, define $B_{\ell,R}:=\ell(2R^2)-\ell(-2R^2)$. Then $0<B_{\ell,R}\le4L_0R^2$.
lem-vector-rademacher-contraction-for-bo:
## Statement

Let $m,d\ge1$, let $V$ be a nonempty bounded subset of $(\mathbb R^d)^m$, and let $h_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be $L$-Lipschitz for one common $L\ge0$. Let $(\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^m$ and $(\eta_{it})_{1\le i\le m,1\le t\le d}$ be independent uniform signs in $\{-1,+1\}$. Writing $v_i=(v_{i1},\ldots,v_{id})$, the one-sided averages satisfy

$$\mathbb E_\varepsilon\sup_{v\in V}\sum_{i=1}^m\varepsilon_i h_i(v_i)\le\sqrt3L\,\mathbb E_\eta\sup_{v\in V}\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{t=1}^d\eta_{it}v_{it}.$$

Neither supremum uses an absolute value, and no condition $h_i(0)=0$ is imposed. The bound holds for finite or infinite bounded $V$; all displayed suprema are finite.
def-latent-class-contrastive-learning:
## Definition

Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal C_0,\rho)$ and $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be measurable probability spaces. For each class $c\in\mathcal C$, let $D_c$ be a probability measure on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ and assume $c\mapsto D_c(A)$ is measurable for every $A\in\mathcal A$. Assume the displayed mixtures define probability measures. The positive-pair law $D_{\rm sim}$ and negative marginal $D_{\rm neg}$ are specified by

$$D_{\rm sim}(A\times B):=\int_{\mathcal C}D_c(A)D_c(B)\,\rho(dc),\qquad D_{\rm neg}(A):=\int_{\mathcal C}D_c(A)\,\rho(dc)$$

for measurable $A,B\in\mathcal A$. Equivalently, draw $C\sim\rho$ and then draw $X,X^+$ independently with law $D_C$ for a positive pair; draw a fresh independent class $C'\sim\rho$ and $X^-\sim D_{C'}$ for one negative. The class labels are latent: the learner observes the pair and negative data, not their classes.

Let $d\ge1$, $R>0$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty class of measurable maps $f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d$ satisfying $\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\lVert f(x)\rVert_2\le R$. Use either one-negative loss $\ell_{\rm h}(t)=(1+t)_+$ or $\ell_{\rm log}(t)=\log_2(1+e^t)$ from the immediately preceding loss-properties lemma. The contrastive score and population loss are

$$q_f(x,x^+,x^-):=f(x)^\top\bigl(f(x^-)-f(x^+)\bigr),\qquad L_{\rm un}(f):=\mathbb E_{(X,X^+)\sim D_{\rm sim},\,X^-\sim D_{\rm neg}}\bigl[\ell(q_f(X,X^+,X^-))\bigr].$$

For $M\ge1$, an observed sample is $S=((x_j,x_j^+,x_j^-))_{j=1}^M$ of $M$ independent triplets with common law $D_{\rm sim}\otimes D_{\rm neg}$, and its empirical loss is $\widehat L_{\rm un}(f):=M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\ell(q_f(x_j,x_j^+,x_j^-))$. For this sample define the unnormalized vector Rademacher complexity

$$\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F):=\mathbb E_\varepsilon\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\sum_{j=1}^M\sum_{t=1}^d\bigl(\varepsilon_{jt0}f_t(x_j)+\varepsilon_{jt+}f_t(x_j^+)+\varepsilon_{jt-}f_t(x_j^-)\bigr),$$

where every $\varepsilon_{jt0},\varepsilon_{jt+},\varepsilon_{jt-}$ is an independent uniform sign. This is the one-sided convention with no absolute value and no $1/M$ factor.

Let $C_+,C_-\sim\rho$ be independent class draws and set $\tau:=\Pr(C_+=C_-)<1$. Assume the diagonal $\Delta:=\{(c,c):c\in\mathcal C\}$ and each $\Delta_A:=\{(c,c):c\in A\}$, $A\in\mathcal C_0$, are measurable. The average binary task draws $(C_+,C_-)$ conditional on $C_+\ne C_-$, then samples a label $Y$ uniformly from $\{+1,-1\}$ and an input $X$ from $D_{C_+}$ if $Y=+1$ or $D_{C_-}$ if $Y=-1$. For a vector representation $f$, a binary linear classifier uses a weight vector $w\in\mathbb R^d$ and loss $\ell(-Yw^\top f(X))$. Define $L_{\rm sup}(f)$ as the average over tasks of the infimum of this risk over $w\in\mathbb R^d$. Write $\mu_c:=\mathbb E_{X\sim D_c}f(X)$ and define the class-mean classifier by $w_\mu=\mu_{C_+}-\mu_{C_-}$; its average risk is $L^\mu_{\rm sup}(f)$. For $\gamma>0$, write $L^\mu_{\gamma,\rm sup}(f)$ for the same mean-classifier risk with margin loss $\ell_\gamma(t):=(1+t/\gamma)_+$ in place of $\ell$.

For $\tau>0$, let $L^=_{\rm un}(f)$ and $L^\ne_{\rm un}(f)$ be the conditional contrastive risks given $C_+=C_-$ and $C_+\ne C_-$, respectively. Let $\nu$ be the class law conditioned on the collision event, namely $\nu(A):=(\rho\otimes\rho)(\Delta_A)/\tau$ for $A\in\mathcal C_0$; for an atomic class law this gives $\nu(\{c\})=\rho(\{c\})^2/\tau$. Define $\Sigma_f(c):=\mathbb E_{X\sim D_c}[(f(X)-\mu_c)(f(X)-\mu_c)^\top]$ and

$$s(f):=\mathbb E_{C\sim\nu}\left[\sqrt{\lVert\Sigma_f(C)\rVert_{\rm op}}\,\mathbb E_{X\sim D_C}\lVert f(X)\rVert_2\right],\qquad \lVert\Sigma\rVert_{\rm op}:=\max_{\lVert u\rVert_2=1}\lVert\Sigma u\rVert_2.$$

The assumed measurability of $\Delta$ and every $\Delta_A$ makes the displayed collision event and conditional class law well-defined; disjoint class sets give disjoint $\Delta_A$, so the formula for $\nu$ is countably additive and has total mass one. Assume also that $c\mapsto\mu_c$ and $c\mapsto\Sigma_f(c)$ are measurable for each $f$, and that the displayed class-conditional risks and random suprema used below are measurable.

If $\tau=0$, there is no collision term; set $s(f):=0$ and use $L_{\rm un}(f)=L^\ne_{\rm un}(f)$. Any empirical minimizer or approximate minimizer used below is separately assumed to be a measurable selector; no selector-existence claim is part of this definition.
lem-mean-classifier-loss-from-contrastiv:
## Statement

Let $C_+,C_-$ be independent with law $\rho$, conditioned on $C_+\ne C_-$, let $X,X^+$ be independent with law $D_{C_+}$, and let $X^-$ be independent with law $D_{C_-}$. For every measurable bounded representation $f$ and either source hinge or logistic loss, the average binary-task mean-classifier risk satisfies

$$L^\mu_{\rm sup}(f)\le L^\ne_{\rm un}(f).$$

Here each binary task uses a uniform label from its two classes, and $L^\ne_{\rm un}$ is the contrastive loss conditional on different positive and negative classes.
lem-contrastive-class-collision-deviatio:
## Statement

In the one-negative latent-class model, for every bounded representation $f$ and either source loss, the population contrastive loss decomposes as

$$L_{\rm un}(f)=\tau L^=_{\rm un}(f)+(1-\tau)L^\ne_{\rm un}(f).$$

If $\tau>0$, the same-class conditional loss obeys

$$1\le L^=_{\rm un}(f)\le1+c_0s(f),\qquad c_0:=\sqrt2\,L_0,$$

where $L_0$ is the common Lipschitz constant of the hinge and logistic losses. If $\tau=0$, then $L_{\rm un}(f)=L^\ne_{\rm un}(f)$ and the model's convention is $s(f)=0$.
lem-subgaussian-contrastive-margin-compa:
## Statement

In the one-negative latent-class model, fix a bounded representation $f$ with $\sup_x\|f(x)\|_2\le R$, where $R>0$. Use the hinge loss $\ell_{\rm h}(t)=(1+t)_+$. Suppose that for every class $c$, the centered vector $f(X)-\mu_c$, for $X\sim D_c$, is sub-Gaussian in every direction with proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, define

$$\gamma:=\begin{cases}1+2R\sigma\sqrt{2\ln R+\ln(3/\epsilon)},&R\ge1,\\1+2R\sigma\sqrt{\ln(3/\epsilon)},&0<R<1.\end{cases}$$

Then the contrastive risk conditioned on distinct positive and negative classes satisfies

$$L^\ne_{\rm un}(f)\le\gamma L^\mu_{\gamma,\rm sup}(f)+\epsilon.$$

This comparison is for the hinge contrastive loss and its scaled hinge mean-classifier risk.
lem-contrastive-uniform-generalization:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the one-negative latent-class model, fix $R>0$, a source loss $\ell\in\{\ell_{\rm h},\ell_{\rm log}\}$, a sample size $M\ge1$, and a sample $S$ of $M$ IID triplets. Assume the loss risks and all sample, independent-copy, and sign suprema below are measurable. Let $B_{\ell,R}=\ell(2R^2)-\ell(-2R^2)$ and define

$$\Gamma_M(S,\delta):=\frac{2\sqrt{18}L_0R\,\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)}{M}+3B_{\ell,R}\sqrt{\frac{\ln(4/\delta)}{2M}},\qquad 0<\delta<1.$$

With probability at least $1-\delta$ over $S$,

$$\forall f\in\mathcal F,\qquad |L_{\rm un}(f)-\widehat L_{\rm un}(f)|\le\Gamma_M(S,\delta).$$

Here $\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)$ is the unnormalized vector Rademacher complexity of the three embeddings in each triplet.
lem-contrastive-empirical-minimizer-exce:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the hypotheses of the one-negative uniform-generalization lemma for a sample $S$ of size $M$. Let $\widehat f$ be a measurable random representation such that, almost surely, $\widehat L_{\rm un}(\widehat f)\le\widehat L_{\rm un}(f)+\eta$ for every $f\in\mathcal F$, where $\eta\ge0$. For every $0<\delta<1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,

$$\forall f\in\mathcal F,\qquad L_{\rm un}(\widehat f)\le L_{\rm un}(f)+2\Gamma_M(S,\delta)+\eta,$$

where

$$\Gamma_M(S,\delta):=\frac{2\sqrt{18}L_0R\,\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)}{M}+3B_{\ell,R}\sqrt{\frac{\ln(4/\delta)}{2M}}$$

is the uniform-deviation quantity for the same sample and loss. The case $\eta=0$ includes any attained measurable empirical minimizer; the statement does not assert that such a selector exists.
thm-contrastive-representation-transfer-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the one-negative latent-class model with $\tau<1$. Fix either source hinge or logistic loss and a sample size $M\ge1$. Suppose all risks and suprema in the uniform-generalization statement are measurable and that a measurable exact empirical minimizer $\widehat f\in\mathcal F$ exists, meaning $\widehat L_{\rm un}(\widehat f)\le\widehat L_{\rm un}(g)$ for every $g\in\mathcal F$ almost surely. For every $0<\delta<1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the IID triplet sample,

$$\forall f\in\mathcal F,\qquad L^\mu_{\rm sup}(\widehat f)\le\frac{L_{\rm un}(f)-\tau+2\Gamma_M(S,\delta)}{1-\tau},$$

where

$$\Gamma_M(S,\delta):=\frac{2\sqrt{18}L_0R\,\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)}{M}+3B_{\ell,R}\sqrt{\frac{\ln(4/\delta)}{2M}}$$

is the uniform-deviation quantity for the same sample and loss. This is a guarantee for the average binary task with a uniform label and the class-mean linear classifier.
cor-contrastive-approximate-erm-transfer:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the one-negative latent-class model with $\tau<1$. Fix either source hinge or logistic loss, a sample size $M\ge1$, and a tolerance $\eta\ge0$. Suppose the risks and suprema in the uniform-generalization statement are measurable and let $\widehat f\in\mathcal F$ be a measurable selector satisfying $\widehat L_{\rm un}(\widehat f)\le\widehat L_{\rm un}(f)+\eta$ for every $f\in\mathcal F$ almost surely. For every $0<\delta<1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,

$$\forall f\in\mathcal F,\qquad L^\mu_{\rm sup}(\widehat f)\le\frac{L_{\rm un}(f)-\tau+2\Gamma_M(S,\delta)+\eta}{1-\tau},$$

where

$$\Gamma_M(S,\delta):=\frac{2\sqrt{18}L_0R\,\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)}{M}+3B_{\ell,R}\sqrt{\frac{\ln(4/\delta)}{2M}}$$

is the uniform-deviation quantity for the same sample and loss. The result assumes such a measurable approximate selector and does not assert its existence.
thm-contrastive-representation-transfer-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the one-negative latent-class model with $\tau<1$. Fix either source hinge or logistic loss, $M\ge1$, and a measurable exact empirical minimizer $\widehat f\in\mathcal F$ satisfying $\widehat L_{\rm un}(\widehat f)\le\widehat L_{\rm un}(g)$ for every $g\in\mathcal F$ almost surely, under the measurability hypotheses of the uniform-generalization result. For each comparator $f\in\mathcal F$ and every $0<\delta<1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the IID triplet sample,

$$L_{\rm sup}(\widehat f)\le L^\mu_{\rm sup}(\widehat f)\le L^\ne_{\rm un}(f)+\frac{\sqrt2L_0\tau s(f)+2\Gamma_M(S,\delta)}{1-\tau},$$

where $L_{\rm sup}$ is the infimum of the average binary-task risk over all linear classifiers, $s(f)$ is the within-class covariance deviation, and

$$\Gamma_M(S,\delta):=\frac{2\sqrt{18}L_0R\,\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)}{M}+3B_{\ell,R}\sqrt{\frac{\ln(4/\delta)}{2M}}$$

is the uniform-deviation quantity for the same sample and loss. The event is simultaneous for all comparators.
cor-subgaussian-contrastive-representati:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the one-negative latent-class model with $\tau<1$. Use the source hinge loss for both contrastive training and the binary mean-classifier task. Fix $M\ge1$, a measurable exact empirical minimizer $\widehat f\in\mathcal F$ satisfying $\widehat L_{\rm un}(\widehat f)\le\widehat L_{\rm un}(g)$ for every $g\in\mathcal F$ almost surely, $0<\delta<1$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$. Let $f\in\mathcal F$ be any comparator whose centered class-conditional representation vectors are sub-Gaussian in every direction with common proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$. Define

$$\gamma:=\begin{cases}1+2R\sigma\sqrt{2\ln R+\ln(3/\epsilon)},&R\ge1,\\1+2R\sigma\sqrt{\ln(3/\epsilon)},&0<R<1.\end{cases}$$

Under the risk and supremum measurability hypotheses, with probability at least $1-\delta$,

$$L_{\rm sup}(\widehat f)\le L^\mu_{\rm sup}(\widehat f)\le\gamma L^\mu_{\gamma,\rm sup}(f)+\epsilon+\frac{\sqrt2L_0\tau s(f)+2\Gamma_M(S,\delta)}{1-\tau}.$$

The uniform-deviation quantity is

$$\Gamma_M(S,\delta):=\frac{2\sqrt{18}L_0R\,\mathcal R_S(\mathcal F)}{M}+3B_{\ell_{\rm h},R}\sqrt{\frac{\ln(4/\delta)}{2M}},$$

where $L^\mu_{\gamma,\rm sup}(f)$ is the average task risk of the class-mean weight $w_\mu$ using the scaled hinge loss $(1-Yw_\mu^\top f(X)/\gamma)_+$. The logistic transfer theorems remain separate; the source margin comparison does not supply their logistic analogue.
